about: Videos and loops of the v5 page (webmedia). Each item: file and poster (relative to this folder), size, seconds, loop, bytes, alt text, a one-line caption, the images or data it was made from, and the script that rebuilds it. H.264 High yuv420p, +faststart, no audio track.

items.alt: Race of four methods making 4096 by 4096 images, shown 20 times faster than real time: in the 202.4 seconds AReA takes for one image, progressive SCA finishes 4, single-pass SCA 2 and HRDiT 1.
items.caption: Clean seconds per 4096 x 4096 image on one GH200 (batch 1), time shown 20x faster. Every lane works through the same prompts: the paper's decile prompts of the ImageReward gain over AReA from the median outward (50th, 60th, 40th, 70th percentile).

queue.prompt: A snow-covered landscape surrounds a cascading waterfall, with icy rocks and a flowing river reflecting the muted light, while chunks of ice float on the water's surface.
Snow-covered landscape featuring a group of sheep in the foreground, with a quaint, snow-dusted church and rustic houses in the background surrounded by trees.

A starry night sky filled with countless stars and the Milky Way stretches across the scene, highlighting rugged, eroded rock formations that rise dramatically from the ground. The landscape features unique, tabletop-like rock structures under soft illumination.

Four men sit on a vintage couch, showcasing vibrant outfits and elaborate accessories. The first wears a gold mask and yellow suit, the second dons blue velvet with a wide-brimmed hat and goggles, the third is clothed in an orange jacket adorned with turquoise jewelry, and the fourth sports a glittery black jacket with round glasses. They hold decorative sticks, set against a backdrop of greenery and warm lighting.

sources.decile_rule: nearest-rank deciles of ImageReward(progressive SCA) - ImageReward(AReA), 195 evaluation prompts, seed 0

items.source: numbers.json main.*.time_clean (= paper headline macros); images: paper decile prompts 50, 60, 40, 70 from the 195-prompt evaluation pool

items.alt: Two panels of the same 4096 by 4096 image with a moving query point: for head 4 the orange window around the query dominates; for head 7 only the blue grid of keys over the whole image carries weight.
items.caption: Each head mixes a native-size window (orange, 64 x 64 tokens around the query's tile) and a native-size grid (blue, 64 x 64 keys over the whole image) by its reach pi. Block 12 at 4096 x 4096: head 4 pi = 0.93, head 7 pi = 0.00 (reach table at r = 4, sigma = 0.62).

sources.geometry: Section 3.1: tile 8, window 64 clamped to the grid, block centres at stride 4

items.source: reach table results/evidence/calib/k1_1024.npz (block 12, heads 4 and 7, r = 4); sheep-church 4096^2

items.alt: Reach emulation at 1024 by 1024: a head's full attention at one query, its window and grid shrinking by a factor of four, and the weight between them sliding along an error parabola until it settles at its minimum.
items.caption: Reach emulation: at 1024 x 1024 both views shrink by r (window 16 tokens, grid stride 4 for r = 4) and the weight that best matches full attention has a closed form, pi* = clip(B/A, 0, 1) = 0.79 for block 12, head 10. Real attention of one query, real sums over 32 prompts.
items.source: attention capture paper/figures/src/data/v6_attn_block12.npz; J sums method_assets/provenance.json

items.alt: A progressive SCA run: the image estimate grows from 1024 to 2048 to 4096 pixels, and a grid of 1,368 head weights lights up in orange and blue once the 2048 and 4096 stages read the reach table.
items.caption: Progressive SCA keeps HRDiT's three stages: 30 steps at 1024 x 1024 with the model's own attention, then 17 at 2048 x 2048 reading the reach table at r = 2 and 10 at 4096 x 4096 at r = 4. Recorded run of the first paper-hero prompt with a trace.

items.alt: Silver braids: a progressive SCA image forming over 57 steps at 1024, 2048 and 4096 pixels. A focus moves across three detailed patches, showing the native-size window and the coarse grid each head reads, while zoomed patches on the right sharpen and end at native pixels.
items.caption: Silver braids: how a 4096 x 4096 image forms with progressive SCA. Orange: the native-size window around a patch; blue: the native-size grid over the whole image; chips: how much two heads use each (positions exact; weights from the reach table). Patches: the run's recorded window and two of highest edge energy.

items.title: Silver braids
captions: The layout forms at the size the model was trained on.
Near-looking heads read a native-size window around each patch.
Far-looking heads read a coarse grid over the whole image, so the layout holds.
Each patch ends at the final image's native pixels.

items.alt: An 86-second explainer without sound, with captions: the problem at 4096 by 4096, the observation that reach belongs to the head, the two native-size views, reach emulation at 1024 by 1024, the three sampler stages, the speed race and the headline results.
items.caption: The method in 86 seconds: reach is a property of the head; measure it once at 1024 x 1024; generate at any size. Captions burned in and in explainer.vtt.

cues.text: FLUX.1-dev at 4096 × 4096 without training: only the attention changes.
FLUX.1-dev is trained near 1024 × 1024, a grid of 64 × 64 tokens.
Run directly at 4096 × 4096, full attention sees 16 times the tokens and offsets up to 255, where training saw 63.
Split one query's keys into near and far: the near share is that head's reach.
Over 1,368 heads and every noise level, which head it is explains 97.5% of the variance.
The noise level explains 2.5%; a schedule shared by all heads, 0.7%.
SCA gives each head two native-size views: a window around the query and a grid over the whole image.
Each head mixes the two by its own reach π.
Measure once at 1024 × 1024, where full attention is still the reference: both views shrink by r.
The best weight has a closed form, π* = clip(B/A, 0, 1), and fills the reach table.
Generate at any size: progressive SCA keeps HRDiT's three sampler stages.
The 2048² and 4096² stages read the same reach table, at r = 2 and r = 4.
49.2 s per 4096² image on one GH200: 4.1× faster than AReA, 2.2× faster than HRDiT.
In AReA's 202.4 s for one image, progressive SCA finishes four.
Better than AReA on all ten per-image metrics, at each of three seeds.
Statistically indistinguishable from HRDiT on three preference scores, in 46% of its time.
A 4096 × 4096 progressive SCA image, from the whole frame to native pixels.
